label: Radon gas in homes
summary: Radon is a radioactive gas from uranium in soil and rock. It seeps into buildings through the foundation and builds up indoors, and you can't see, smell or taste it. Breathed for years it causes lung cancer: Health Canada ranks it second only to smoking and first in people who have never smoked, links it to about 16% of Canada's lung cancer deaths, and sets a guideline of 200 Bq/m³ as a yearly average; a 2024 survey estimated about 1 home in 5 is above it.
signs: Nothing you can sense: almost every home has some radon, and similar houses next door to each other can differ widely. Only a test shows the level
Basements and crawl spaces usually have the most, being nearest the soil and poorly ventilated. The lowest floor people live on is the one that counts
Ways in: cracks in foundation floors and walls, floor-to-wall joints, gaps around pipes and posts, floor drains, sumps, and bare soil or rock in cellars and crawl spaces
Cold months: with windows and doors shut, levels are typically higher. Fireplaces and exhaust fans change the air pressure in the house and can draw more radon in from the soil
No part of Canada is radon-free. In parts of New Brunswick and Manitoba over 40% of homes tested were above the guideline, and in Castlegar, BC and Regina, Sask., over half
do: To know the level, test for at least 3 months, best through the heating season, with a long-term detector or digital monitor on the lowest floor someone uses 4 hours a day or more, 0.5–2 m off the floor, away from windows, doors, vents, outside walls and heat

Go by the long-term average only. Above 200 Bq/m³ (5.4 pCi/L on monitors set to US units), Health Canada says fix it within a year, sooner if higher; below that the risk is small, but no level is risk-free
Until it's fixed or tested low, sleep and spend your long hours on upper floors, and keep basement time short. Upper floors usually have less, but high radon can turn up anywhere in a home

Seal cracks and joints in foundation floors and walls and gaps around pipes, fit an airtight cover on an open sump, and keep floor-drain traps full of water; a skim of cooking oil slows drying. Sealing helps but won't fix high radon on its own
Air the house out: open windows and doors for a through-draught when you can. An HRV or air exchanger run all the time, with intake and exhaust balanced, cuts radon by about 20–50%
If the house has a radon system (a sealed pipe from under the basement floor to outside, with a fan), keep the fan running whenever you have power: it cuts radon by 90% or more
dont: Don't trust a short reading: radon changes day to day, so a few days or weeks can read far higher or lower than the yearly average. Health Canada doesn't recommend tests shorter than 91 days
Don't rely on a digital monitor that isn't on C-NRPP's approved list: many models are marked not approved, and several were recalled by Health Canada
Don't put a test in a kitchen, bathroom, laundry room, closet or crawl space, or by a sump or open crack: it won't show what you breathe where you live

Don't leave exhaust fans running for long in a closed-up house: pulling air out lowers the pressure indoors, draws more soil gas in through the floor, and can pull smoke and exhaust back from a stove or furnace (see Carbon monoxide)
ppe: What protects is a lower radon level and fewer hours in the lowest rooms; a test is the only way to know whether you need either

A digital radon monitor on C-NRPP's approved list, such as Airthings Corentium Home, Wave Plus or View Plus, or Ecosense RadonEye, EcoQube or EcoBlu. They can't be professionally recalibrated, and Health Canada suggests replacing one after about 5 years
A mail-in long-term kit (alpha track) is read by a lab: the detector goes back after 3 months, and results take 3 to 6 weeks
firstAid: Nothing shows at the time: radon gives no warning, and lung cancer from it can take many years to appear. What helps is less exposure from now on

Smoking makes it far worse: for a lifetime at 200 Bq/m³, Health Canada puts lung cancer risk at about 2% for non-smokers and 17% for smokers (12% from smoking alone). Less smoking and second-hand smoke helps most where you can't lower the radon
A high reading isn't an emergency: the risk builds with the level and the years you breathe it. Move sleeping upstairs, and seal and air the lowest floor while you work out a fix
